system.name: UEO (Universal Entropy Optimization) for U2-FT
system.one_liner: A CLIP fine-tuning setting with imprecise class names and unknown-class data, solved by entropy optimisation of the prompt and affine transforms.

content.variant_note: two grey panels side by side, a train phase drawn as a small pipeline and a test phase drawn as a sketch of known and unknown classes
content.argues: Fine-tuning CLIP on unlabeled in-the-wild data with an imprecise class-name list should improve both recognition of known classes (generalization) and detection of unknown classes (OOD).
content.subject: The U2-FT setup: class names and unlabeled photo sets C1 and C2 feed CLIP encoders, similarity and fine-tuning; the test set mixes known and unknown classes.

layout.arrangement_note: Two grey rounded panels side by side. The left Train Phase panel holds a small left-to-right pipeline (class tags and prompt on top, two dashed photo sets below, two 3D encoder boxes, a similarity box and a large fine-tuning box). The right Test Phase panel holds a green circle with photos and dashed class boundaries, two outliers outside it, two goal tags with smileys and a two-row colour legend. Each panel is titled at its bottom right.

lessons.what_to_learn: State a new learning setting as two grey panels (train, test): show the imprecise inputs as thumbnails framed by known or unknown colour, the method as a few boxes, and the test goal as a tinted circle with dashed boundaries and outliers tagged with the two goals.
lessons.suits: Problem-setting figures for open-set, OOD, partial-label or universal learning, where the point is what the data contains (known versus unknown classes) rather than the architecture.

evidence: U2-FT fine-tunes the pre-trained CLIP with unlabeled in-the-wild training data according to an imprecise predefined list of class names
a training-independent data set containing both known classes and unknown classes (OOD) in the test phase is employed

summary: The paper introduces Unsupervised Universal Fine-Tuning (U2-FT), a realistic way to adapt CLIP when the predefined class names are imprecise and the unlabeled data contains unknown classes, and proposes Universal Entropy Optimization (UEO). Figure 1 shows the setup in two grey panels. In the Train Phase, four class-name tags (fox, dog, cat, pig) are merged into the prompt 'a photo of a [class]' for a text-encoder box, unlabeled animal photos in two dashed sets C1 and C2 go to an image-encoder box, and both meet in a similarity box that feeds an 'unsupervised universal fine-tuning' box. In the Test Phase, photos sit in a green circle cut by dashed class boundaries, with outliers (panda, tiger) outside, tagged Generalization and OOD Detection with smileys; teal and red frames mark known and unknown classes.
summary_zh: 论文提出U2-FT设定：预设类名可能不准、无标注数据含未知类，并给出UEO方法。图1分训练与测试两块：训练阶段由类名提示与C1、C2图片经编码器和相似度进入微调；测试阶段圆内为已知类，圆外熊猫、白虎为未知类。
notes: The figure draws the setting (U2-FT), not the UEO objective itself. Prior kinds kept. The digest counts 14 placed bitmaps (12 photo placements plus two items I judged to be the smileys, which I recorded as vector because the digest lists only 10 different bitmaps, matching the 10 distinct photos); the smiley medium is therefore uncertain.
